Subject: Questions on tracking, telemetry and DPA for BrightReview POC

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost breakdowns were really helpful. Before we progress to a POC, our privacy team has a few specific questions we need cleared up around the marketing pixels/analytics we plan to run and how telemetry from your console is handled. High-level asks:

- For the website tags we plan to deploy, do you act as a data processor for the collected analytics/marketing cookies, or is that purely BrightReview's responsibility?
- Are the cookies/SDK events sent to Redwood stored or retained in identifiable form (IP, full user-agent, device IDs)? If so, what's the default retention and is it configurable per account?
- Can you provide your current list of subprocessors and confirm whether any are outside the EU/UK (we need details on data transfer mechanisms: SCCs, EU-US frameworks, or equivalent).
- Do you have recommended cookie banner language for marketing analytics that references Redwood as a processor (we'll need to show this in our consent capture docs)?

I can loop in our external privacy counsel (Marco Ruiz) if that helps for DPA/subprocessor legal details. Appreciate a concise write-up we can share with legal — we're hoping to get contractual terms started next week.

Best,
Olivia
Director, Growth — BrightReview Inc

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Laura (Customer Success) to address the specifics; I pulled our latest DPA and subprocessors list and attached them. Quick answers up-front:

- Processor role: Redwood acts as processor for any telemetry or analytics events customers route to our hosted telemetry/analytics endpoint. If you deploy tags that send data only to BrightReview systems (not our hosted analytics), Redwood is not a processor for those events.

- Retention & identifiers: by default we store telemetry events for 90 days, with tokenized identifiers; IPs are hashed and user-agent strings are truncated to family + major version. We can customize retention windows for enterprise customers (30/90/365 days) under Dedicated/Private plans.

- Subprocessors & transfers: attached is the subprocessors list (current as of May 2026). We do use cloud CDN/logging providers in the US and EU; transfers are covered by SCCs and our Data Processing Agreement includes the EU SCC addendum. For UK transfers we rely on the UK Addendum.

- Cookie banner text: we have sample language but need to confirm the exact copy depending on whether you declare Redwood as a processor. Marissa — can you confirm the short banner snippet and DPA clause?

I'll set up a 30-minute sync with Marco if you want to walk legal through the attachments.

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi all — thanks for the context. A few clarifying points from legal so we can produce definitive language for your privacy team:

1) Scope of processing: please confirm which of the following BrightReview will do during the POC so we can mark the roles in the DPA: page view events + marketing tags (browser), signup form submissions (PII), console telemetry (admin actions). If you intend to route PII (names/emails) into Redwood for enrichment/embedding, that changes the clause set.

2) Identifiers and pseudonymization: Karthik's note on IP hashing and UA truncation aligns with our standard. We need to confirm whether BrightReview requires raw IP retention for fraud detection — if so, we will need a contract exception and a separate dataflow diagram.

3) Subprocessors and transfer mechanisms: attached subprocessors list shows providers in US, EU, and India. For EU/UK-covered data, we rely on SCCs (model clauses) with customer-binding addenda. If BrightReview is subject to stricter local rules (e.g., Germany BDSG interpretations) please flag and we'll provide regional contracts.

4) Cookie/banner language: proposed short line for consent UI (suggested): "We use cookies and external analytics (including processing by our vendor Redwood Inference) to improve our site and marketing. Manage preferences or accept." Marissa — note to self: provide a second variant that does not mention vendor by name for marketing-led banners.

5) Retention and deletion: standard 90 days for general telemetry; 30 days available for analytics-only buckets. We can provide API calls for on-demand deletion (subject to contractual SLA). Please confirm desired retention and whether you need a delete API.

Next steps I propose: BrightReview to confirm the POC dataflows (checkbox form), Redwood to provide a short DPA redline and a template cookie banner copy. Marco — if you'd like to review the DPA redline, we can schedule a 30-minute call Monday.

Regards,
Marissa Cole

- Transfers: SCCs cover EU transfers; UK Addendum is available. Subprocessors list attached (we will update if any changes before contract).
